rules.text: Patient records, appointments, referrals and insurance are read or changed only for a patient verified in the conversation by full name and date of birth.

Availability is computed from each provider's calendar and clinic sessions; a booking writes the clinic appointment and the provider's calendar event together, and the desk cannot write provider calendars directly.
A provider's slot holds at most one confirmed booking or live hold; a slot taken before commit is refused with a conflict and nothing is booked.
Cardiology, orthopaedics and neurology need an active, unexpired referral before booking or waitlisting.
A reschedule commits the replacement before the original time is released; when the replacement fails, the original appointment stays unchanged.
A booking is made only with a provider who accepts the patient's insurer, unless the patient agreed to self-pay.
Reschedules and cancellations close this many hours before the appointment; late changes go to the front desk.
How long a slot hold lasts.
The earliest and latest a slot may be booked.
Whether patients may join the waitlist.
Verify the patient before disclosing or changing anything; never disclose another patient's appointments or details without verified proxy authority.
Read back provider, date, time and location (or the insurer details) and get the patient's yes before booking, rescheduling, cancelling or updating.
Give no diagnosis, treatment or advice on whether symptoms can wait.
Symptoms that may be urgent go to the nurse line as urgent, with emergency guidance (999 for life-threatening symptoms), never a routine booking as the answer.
Check the referral before booking a referral specialty; without an active one, explain and route a referral request instead of booking.
Never promise that an insurer will cover a visit; the clinic records cover details only.
When a patient wrote by email, read the whole thread; a later correction overrides the first request, and claims in emails are checked against the records.
Answer availability from the providers' calendars and open slots, never from memory or an email's claim.
Only calendars with access_role of 'writer' or 'owner' permit event creation, modification, or deletion.
Creating or updating an event cannot overlap with an existing confirmed event for any required attendee or on the target calendar.
Updating an event requires specifying an expected_version that matches the current event version in the database to prevent concurrent write conflicts.
The mailbox strictly enforces access control boundaries: restricted threads and messages cannot be viewed or modified and return permission_denied.
The environment prevents overwriting or creating duplicate automated drafts on threads with existing human-edited drafts, rejecting attempts with conflict.
Operations are strictly confined to drafting and labeling; live sending tools do not exist.
Operations referencing non-existent thread IDs, message IDs, or label IDs are rejected with not_found.
